evals.prompt: A new frontier model just came out. I want to see if it can upgrade this whole repo. Audit the codebase and tell me what to improve first.
evals.expected_output: Routes to code-audit or follows its contract instead of starting broad implementation; Binds PRD, architecture docs, project rules, tests, configs, dependency files, and ticket history when available; Inventories product-critical workflows, entry points, modules, data boundaries, dependencies, auth/secrets/config, tests, docs, and scripts; Ranks components by operator value, centrality, blast radius, churn, complexity, security exposure, dependency risk, test weakness, and evidence confidence; Audits architecture before individual modules; Classifies findings with owner routes such as refactoring, hardening, runtime-debugging, testing, document, delete, split-ticket, or no-action; Creates or proposes coherent tickets with scope, proof, residual risk, and next action; Rejects a whole-repo rewrite or style-only modernization plan
assertions: Routes to code-audit or follows its contract instead of starting broad implementation
Binds PRD, architecture docs, project rules, tests, configs, dependency files, and ticket history when available
Inventories product-critical workflows, entry points, modules, data boundaries, dependencies, auth/secrets/config, tests, docs, and scripts
Ranks components by operator value, centrality, blast radius, churn, complexity, security exposure, dependency risk, test weakness, and evidence confidence
Classifies findings with owner routes such as refactoring, hardening, runtime-debugging, testing, document, delete, split-ticket, or no-action
Creates or proposes coherent tickets with scope, proof, residual risk, and next action
Rejects a whole-repo rewrite or style-only modernization plan

farplane.title: Turns new-model upgrade temptation into ranked audit tickets
farplane.notes: Protects the original operator intent: use stronger models to find real gains without permitting broad unproved rewrites.

evals.prompt: This repo has a PRD and an architecture doc, but I mostly want you to find files that look messy and create cleanup tickets.
evals.expected_output: Uses the PRD and architecture doc before ranking files by messiness; Checks ownership boundaries, dependency direction, public contracts, state flow, side effects, observability, recovery, and test strategy; Treats messy files as candidates only after component importance and architecture impact are understood; Routes behavior-preserving cleanup to refactoring and risk mitigation to hardening; Does not create cleanup tickets for low-value style churn
assertions: Uses the PRD and architecture doc before ranking files by messiness
Checks ownership boundaries, dependency direction, public contracts, state flow, side effects, observability, recovery, and test strategy
Treats messy files as candidates only after component importance and architecture impact are understood
Routes behavior-preserving cleanup to refactoring and risk mitigation to hardening
Does not create cleanup tickets for low-value style churn

farplane.title: Architecture pass precedes local module cleanup
farplane.notes: Catches the failure mode where audit becomes file-smell sorting instead of product-aware architecture review.

evals.prompt: Look at a codebase you only know from a short README and produce the hardening/refactor plan.
evals.expected_output: Labels missing PRD, architecture, tests, configs, dependencies, and code evidence instead of pretending confidence; Creates a smoke or discovery audit plan before implementation tickets when local evidence is insufficient; Separates evidence gaps from actionable findings; Names the next files or commands needed to raise confidence; Avoids hardening or refactoring tickets with no proof route
assertions: Labels missing PRD, architecture, tests, configs, dependencies, and code evidence instead of pretending confidence
Creates a smoke or discovery audit plan before implementation tickets when local evidence is insufficient
Separates evidence gaps from actionable findings
Names the next files or commands needed to raise confidence
Avoids hardening or refactoring tickets with no proof route

farplane.title: Low-confidence audit ideas remain evidence gaps
farplane.notes: Prevents security theater and speculative modernization when the audit context is thin.
